label: Buddhism
blurb: The path of the Buddha: seeing suffering, its cause in craving, and its ending, through virtue, meditation and wisdom.

label: Theravāda
blurb: The oldest surviving Buddhist school, rooted in the Pāli discourses and the monastic code; strong today in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.

label: Early suttas
blurb: Practice read straight from the early discourses, outside the commentarial mainstream; Hillside Hermitage belongs here, drawing on Ñāṇavīra Thera.

label: Thai Forest
blurb: The forest monastic lineage of Ajahn Mun and Ajahn Chah.

label: Insight meditation
blurb: The modern vipassanā movement and its Western retreat centres.

label: Mahāyāna
blurb: The "great vehicle": the bodhisattva ideal of awakening for the sake of all beings, and the teaching of emptiness.

label: Zen
blurb: Chan and Zen: awakening through sitting, direct pointing and the teacher–student encounter, more than through scripture.

label: Vajrayāna
blurb: Tantric Buddhism: deity practice, mantra and the teacher's transmission as a swift path to awakening.

label: Tibetan Buddhism
blurb: The Buddhism of the Himalaya, joining monastic study and debate with Vajrayāna practice and guidance for the dying.

label: Hindu traditions
blurb: The many paths that grew from the Vedas and Upanishads: knowledge, devotion, yoga and action.

label: Vedānta
blurb: Philosophy built on the Upanishads, the Bhagavad Gītā and the Brahma Sūtras, asking how the self relates to Brahman.

label: Advaita Vedānta
blurb: Non-dual Vedānta: the Self (ātman) is Brahman, and the world of separate selves is an appearance.

label: Inchegeri Sampradaya
blurb: The Navnath line of Siddharameshwar and Nisargadatta Maharaj.

label: Ramakrishna Order
blurb: The monastic order founded on Ramakrishna's teaching and Vivekananda's mission: Vedānta lived as service.

label: Kashmir Shaivism
blurb: A non-dual Tantric philosophy in which the world is the free, conscious play of Shiva, recognised as one's own self.

label: Kriya Yoga
blurb: The line of Mahavatar Babaji, Lahiri Mahasaya and Paramahansa Yogananda.

label: Christian traditions
blurb: The traditions that follow Jesus of Nazareth, from the Gospels and the early Church to the mystics.

label: Christian mysticism
blurb: Christians who sought direct union with God: detachment, contemplative prayer and the birth of God in the soul.

label: Gnosticism
blurb: Early Christian and related movements of saving knowledge (gnosis); known mostly through texts such as the Nag Hammadi library.

label: Platonic tradition
blurb: Philosophy as the care of the soul, turning from the world of change toward the eternal Forms and the Good.

label: Neoplatonism
blurb: Late antique Platonism: everything flows from the One, and the soul can return to it through contemplation.

label: Renaissance Platonism
blurb: The revival of Plato and Plotinus in fifteenth-century Florence, joining Platonic philosophy with Christian faith.

label: Western esotericism
blurb: Western paths of hidden knowledge: Hermeticism, Theosophy, Anthroposophy and the Fourth Way.

label: Theosophy
blurb: The movement of Blavatsky and the Theosophical Society, joining Eastern ideas of karma and rebirth with Western occultism.

label: Anthroposophy
blurb: Rudolf Steiner's spiritual science: a path of clear thinking toward knowledge of spiritual worlds, karma and repeated earth lives.

label: The Fourth Way
blurb: Gurdjieff's path of self-remembering and conscious effort in the middle of ordinary life.

label: Independent
blurb: Teachers who stand outside any tradition.

label: Direct path
blurb: The non-dual enquiry into experience taught by Atmananda Krishna Menon and carried on by Jean Klein, Francis Lucille and Rupert Spira.

label: Arsha Vidya
blurb: Traditional teaching of Advaita Vedanta through the texts, in the line of Swami Dayananda Saraswati (Arsha Vidya Gurukulam, Q4796497).

label: Modern non-dual teachers
blurb: Contemporary teachers of awakening who draw on Zen, Advaita and other sources without belonging to one lineage.

label: Plum Village
blurb: Thich Nhat Hanh's Vietnamese Thiền community of engaged, mindful living.

label: Sōtō Zen
blurb: Dōgen's school of just-sitting (shikantaza); San Francisco Zen Center, Sanshin.

label: Rinzai Zen
blurb: The koan school of Japanese Zen; Zen Studies Society.

label: Gelug
blurb: The Tibetan school of Tsongkhapa, headed in practice by the Dalai Lamas.

label: Burmese meditation lineages
blurb: Myanmar's modern meditation schools: Mahasi noting, Pa-Auk samatha-vipassanā, U Ba Khin and Goenka.

label: Krishnamurti
blurb: J. Krishnamurti's teaching after he left Theosophy in 1929: no path, no authority, freedom from the known.

label: Anandamayi Ma Sangha
blurb: The ashrams and monastics around Anandamayi Ma (Shree Shree Anandamayee Sangha, Kankhal and Varanasi), devotional and non-sectarian.

label: Divine Life Society
blurb: The order founded by Swami Sivananda in Rishikesh, carried on by Swami Chidananda.

label: Siddha Yoga
blurb: Guru-yoga path founded by Swami Muktananda in the line of Bhagawan Nityananda: shaktipat, chanting and meditation, drawing on Kashmir Shaiva texts.

label: Goenka Vipassana (U Ba Khin line)
blurb: Lay Vipassana in the line of Ledi Sayadaw, Saya Thetgyi and U Ba Khin, taught by S. N. Goenka in 10-day dana-funded courses.

label: Kagyu
blurb: Tibetan school of the mahamudra lineage from Tilopa and Naropa through Marpa and Milarepa, led by the Karmapas.

label: Nyingma
blurb: The oldest Tibetan school, tracing to Padmasambhava, home of Dzogchen.

label: Sufism
blurb: The inner, mystical path of Islam: remembrance of God (dhikr), the master and the order, the poetry of love.

label: Jewish mysticism
blurb: Merkavah, Kabbalah, the Zohar and Hasidism: the contemplative and mystical currents of Judaism.

label: Philosophy of the sacred
blurb: Contemporary philosophers and scientists on consciousness, meaning and the sacred: idealism, the divided brain, the meaning crisis, perennialism.

label: Modern Paganism
blurb: Druidry, Wicca, Heathenry and goddess spirituality: nature-centred traditions revived or founded in the modern era.

label: Sikhism
blurb: The path of the ten Gurus and the Guru Granth Sahib: remembrance of the one Name, honest work and sharing.

label: Śaivism
blurb: Umbrella for Śiva-centred traditions: the ascetic Atimārga and the initiatory Mantramārga.

label: Pāśupata (Atimārga)
blurb: Earliest Śaiva ascetic order; ash, feigned madness, provoking censure.

label: Śaiva Siddhānta
blurb: Mainstream ritual Śaivism of the Mantramārga; Sanskrit āgamas, later the Tamil Śaiva temple tradition. Kauai Aadheenam teaches a monistic form.

label: Trika
blurb: Abhinavagupta's synthesis around the Mālinīvijayottara; Tantrāloka.

label: Pratyabhijñā (Recognition)
blurb: Philosophical school: liberation as recognising oneself as Śiva.

label: Spanda (Vibration)
blurb: Śiva Sūtras and Spanda Kārikās: consciousness as pulsation.

label: Krama / Kālīkula (Mahārtha)
blurb: Kālī-centred phases (krama) of cognition; Twelve Kālīs.

label: Śāktism
blurb: Goddess-centred traditions; parent of Kaula, Śrī Vidyā and Kālī lines.

label: Śākta practice (Kālī, Kāmākhyā, Bhairavī)
blurb: Bucket for living goddess practice not tied to a single classical school (Kāmākhyā upāsanā, Linga Bhairavi, Daśa Mahāvidyā).

label: Śrī Vidyā
blurb: Worship of Lalitā Tripurasundarī through the Śrī Chakra and the fifteen-syllable mantra.

label: Nāth / Siddha Siddhānta
blurb: Nāth yogī order (Gorakhnāth); Siddha Siddhānta Paddhati; alchemy and haṭha.

label: Haṭha Yoga (premodern)
blurb: Physical-yogic methods first set out in Vajrayāna and Śaiva circles (Amṛtasiddhi, Dattātreyayogaśāstra, Haṭhapradīpikā).

label: Tantra studies (academic)
blurb: Not a tradition: a field tag for scholarly lectures (philology, history).

label: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)
blurb: Includes Amaravati, Chithurst/Cittaviveka, Abhayagiri, Bodhinyana/BSWA, Wat Pah Nanachat, Wat Marp Jan, Wat Boonyawad, Tisarana, Birken.

label: Dhammayut forest line (Ajahn Mun → Maha Boowa / Ajaan Lee)
blurb: Note: Ajahn Dtun, listed by the brief under this line, was ordained by Ajahn Chah (Mahānikāya) and is filed under chah-line.

label: Pa-Auk (samatha-first, Abhidhamma)
blurb: No usable official English short talks found this pass.

label: Mogok Sayadaw (dependent origination)
blurb: Official channel is Burmese-language only; no English clips.

label: Sri Lankan Theravāda (forest & scholastic)
blurb: Hillside Hermitage is already deep in app (early-suttas).

label: Buddhist studies (academic)
blurb: Scholarly lineage node: edges are academic_supervisor_of.

label: Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres
blurb: Swami Vishnudevananda's international centres teaching his guru Sivananda's yoga.

label: Bihar School of Yoga (Satyananda Yoga)
blurb: Yoga of Swami Satyananda, disciple of Sivananda, and the Bihar School of Yoga.

label: Gaudiya Vaishnava (Chaitanya / ISKCON)
blurb: Krishna devotion in the line of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

label: Hindu studies (academic)
blurb: Scholarly lineage node.

label: Dzogchen (Great Perfection)
blurb: Teaching and practice lineage, not a separate institution; also held in Bön and taught across Rimé.

label: Karma Kagyu
blurb: Largest Kagyu branch, led by the Karmapas.

label: Drikung Kagyu
blurb: Founded by Jigten Sumgön.

label: Drukpa Kagyu
blurb: State tradition of Bhutan.

label: Shangpa Kagyu
blurb: Separate lineage from Niguma and Sukhasiddhi, revived by Kalu Rinpoche.

label: Mahamudra (the Great Seal)
blurb: Practice lineage at the heart of Kagyu, also taught in Gelug.

label: Sakya
blurb: Lamdre (path and its fruit) teachings; led by the Khön family.

label: FPMT (Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition)
blurb: International Gelug network founded by Lama Yeshe and Lama Zopa.

label: Jonang
blurb: Known for shentong (other-emptiness) and Kalachakra; suppressed in central Tibet in the 17th c. and survives in Amdo.

label: Bön (Yungdrung Bön)
blurb: Tibet's indigenous religion. It is not a Buddhist school, but it shares its institutions and Dzogchen with Buddhism. Placed here for browsing only.

label: Rimé (non-sectarian) movement
blurb: An ecumenical revival across Nyingma, Kagyu, Sakya and Jonang, not a school.

label: Shambhala
blurb: Trungpa's secular "warrior" path; Pema Chödrön trained in it.

label: Chan
blurb: Chinese meditation school, root of Zen, Seon and Thiền.

label: Linji (Rinzai) line of Chan
blurb: Huatou / gong'an practice.

label: Caodong (Soto) line of Chan
blurb: Silent illumination (mozhao).

label: Dharma Drum Mountain
blurb: Taiwanese Chan organisation of Sheng Yen holding both Linji and Caodong lines.

label: Sanbo Zen (Sanbo Kyodan)
blurb: Lay-oriented school combining Soto and Rinzai koan curricula.

label: White Plum Asanga
blurb: Maezumi's lineage network (Soto with Rinzai koan study).

label: Seon (Korean Zen)
blurb: Korean Chan; Jogye order; Kwan Um School in the West.

label: Kwan Um School of Zen
blurb: International Seon school of Seung Sahn.

label: Thiền
blurb: Vietnamese Chan; Plum Village is its best-known modern form.

label: Order of Buddhist Contemplatives
blurb: Shasta Abbey tradition founded by Houn Jiyu-Kennett.

label: Ordinary Mind Zen
blurb: Joko Beck's psychologically oriented lineage.

label: Tiantai
blurb: Lotus Sutra school; threefold truth; zhiguan (calming and contemplation).

label: Tendai
blurb: Japanese Tiantai, which also includes esoteric (taimitsu), Pure Land and Zen elements.

label: Huayan (Kegon)
blurb: Avatamsaka school; interpenetration of all phenomena.

label: Pure Land
blurb: Devotion to Amitabha and rebirth in Sukhavati.

label: Jōdo-shū
blurb: Honen's school.

label: Jōdo Shinshū (Shin Buddhism)
blurb: Shinran's school; Buddhist Churches of America in the US.

label: East Asian esoteric Buddhism
blurb: Chinese Zhenyan and its Japanese heirs.

label: Shingon
blurb: Kukai's esoteric school.

label: Western magic
blurb: Ritual and initiatory magic in the Hermetic and Qabalistic line: the Golden Dawn, Thelema, the Inner Light.

label: Akbarian school (Ibn Arabi)
blurb: Study and practice centred on Ibn 'Arabi's teaching of the unity of being, as at Beshara.

label: Naqshbandi-Haqqani order
blurb: Sufi order known for silent remembrance (dhikr) and tracing its chain through Abu Bakr.

label: Inayatiyya (universal Sufism, Chishti roots)
blurb: Universal Sufism of Hazrat Inayat Khan, founded in London around 1914-1917.

label: Christian Meditation (John Main / WCCM)
blurb: Contemplative prayer with a single prayer word, taught by John Main and the World Community for Christian Meditation.

label: Franciscan contemplative (Rohr / CAC)
blurb: Followers of St Francis; in the UK including the Anglican Society of St Francis.

label: Orthodox hesychasm
blurb: Eastern Orthodox prayer of inner stillness and the Jesus Prayer.

label: Kabbalah (theosophical and ecstatic)
blurb: Jewish mystical tradition of the sefirot and the hidden meanings of Torah; also its modern popular forms.

label: Druidry
blurb: Modern Druid spirituality of nature, the seasonal festivals and bardic arts, as in OBOD.

label: Wicca
blurb: Modern pagan witchcraft publicised by Gerald Gardner from the 1950s, with covens, the Goddess and God and the wheel of the year.

label: Heathenry
blurb: Modern revival of pre-Christian Germanic and Norse religion (Asatru, Odinism).

label: Goddess spirituality
blurb: Devotion to the divine feminine as Goddess, centred in the UK on Glastonbury.

label: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn
blurb: Initiatory order founded in London in 1888 that shaped modern Western magic.

label: Thelema
blurb: Aleister Crowley's religious and magical system ("Do what thou wilt").

label: Quakers (Religious Society of Friends)
blurb: Christian movement begun by George Fox in 1652, worshipping in expectant silence.

label: Benedictine monasticism
blurb: Monastic life under the Rule of St Benedict.

label: Cistercians (Trappists)
blurb: Reformed Benedictines; Trappists are the Strict Observance.

label: Carmelites
blurb: Contemplative order of Teresa of Avila and John of the Cross.

label: Ignatian spirituality
blurb: The Jesuit way of the Spiritual Exercises of Ignatius of Loyola.

label: Celtic Christianity
blurb: The early Christianity of Britain and Ireland (Columba, Aidan, Cuthbert, David) and its modern revival.

label: Triratna Buddhist Community
blurb: Western Buddhist movement founded by Sangharakshita in London in 1967 (formerly FWBO).

label: New Kadampa Tradition
blurb: Movement founded by Kelsang Gyatso in England, presenting itself as independent of the Tibetan schools (Gelug-derived; contested).

label: Order of Buddhist Contemplatives (Serene Reflection)
blurb: Soto Zen order founded by Jiyu-Kennett, seated at Shasta Abbey and Throssel Hole.

label: Nipponzan-Myohoji
blurb: Japanese Nichiren order of Nichidatsu Fujii that builds peace pagodas.

label: ISKCON (Hare Krishna)
blurb: International Society for Krishna Consciousness, founded by A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada in 1966.

label: Swaminarayan Sampradaya
blurb: Vaishnava tradition of Swaminarayan, including BAPS.

label: Brahma Kumaris
blurb: Spiritual movement founded in Sindh in the 1930s, teaching Raja Yoga meditation; headquarters at Mount Abu.

label: Transcendental Meditation
blurb: Mantra meditation of Maharishi Mahesh Yogi.

label: Swedenborgianism
blurb: Thought and church following the visions of Emanuel Swedenborg.

label: Spiritualism
blurb: Movement based on communication with the dead through mediums.

label: Kaula / Kula
blurb: Clan (kula) cults of yoginīs and Bhairava; source of many later Śākta and haṭha practices.
